name: getent
desc: Query NSS databases such as passwd, group, and hosts.
tip: Use it when the question asks for account fields from the configured identity sources.

name: id
desc: Display UID, GID, and group memberships.
tip: Unlike getent passwd, id focuses on numeric identity and memberships.

name: useradd
tip: Remember -m creates the home directory.

name: usermod
tip: Exam trap: -G without -a replaces supplementary groups.

name: passwd
desc: Set, lock, unlock, or inspect password status.
tip: -l locks password authentication; it does not necessarily terminate existing sessions.

name: chage
tip: Use -l to list aging settings.

name: chmod
tip: 755 gives owner rwx and group/others r-x.

name: chown
tip: chmod changes permissions; chown changes ownership.

name: chgrp
tip: Use chgrp when only the group must change.

name: umask
desc: Control default permission bits removed at creation.
tip: Typical base permissions: files 666, directories 777, then subtract the mask.

name: setfacl
tip: Default ACLs apply to newly created children.

name: getfacl
tip: Use this to verify effective ACL entries.

name: find
tip: Newly created file clues usually point to find, not locate.

name: locate
tip: Fast, but results can be stale until updatedb runs.

name: grep
tip: -i ignores case; -R searches recursively.

name: awk
tip: Think columns and fields.

name: sed
tip: Without -i, sed normally writes transformed output to stdout.

name: cut
desc: Extract selected fields or character positions.
tip: Use -d with -f for delimited fields.

name: sort
tip: -n selects numeric sorting.

name: uniq
tip: uniq only detects adjacent duplicates, so sort first.

name: tee
desc: Write stdin to both stdout and files.
tip: Useful when shell redirection would not inherit sudo.

name: cp
tip: -a preserves metadata and recursively copies.

name: mv
tip: Within one filesystem, mv generally renames directory entries.

name: ln
tip: Hard links cannot cross filesystems; symbolic links can.

name: tar
tip: c=create, x=extract, t=list, f=archive filename.

name: rsync
tip: A trailing slash changes whether the source directory itself or its contents are copied.

name: dd
examples: sudo dd if=/dev/sda of=disk.img bs=4M status=progress
tip: Double-check if= and of=; reversing them can destroy data.

name: dnf
tip: dnf resolves dependencies; rpm works directly with package files.

name: rpm
desc: Query or manage individual RPM packages.
tip: -q queries; -ql lists files in an installed package.

name: apt
tip: update refreshes metadata; upgrade installs available updates.

name: dpkg
tip: dpkg does not automatically resolve repository dependencies.

name: systemctl
tip: start=now; enable=boot; --now combines both.

name: journalctl
tip: -u filters by unit; -b limits to a boot.

name: ps
tip: aux is BSD-style; -ef is UNIX-style.

name: top
desc: Interactively display processes and resource use.
tip: Use load, CPU, memory, and process state together to identify bottlenecks.

name: kill
desc: Send a signal to a process ID.
tip: TERM requests graceful shutdown; KILL cannot be handled.

name: pkill
desc: Signal processes selected by name or attributes.
tip: Use carefully because it may match multiple processes.

name: nice
desc: Start a process with a selected nice value.
tip: Higher nice value means lower CPU priority.

name: renice
desc: Change the nice value of a running process.
tip: Negative nice values normally require elevated privileges.

name: ip
tip: Use ip addr for addresses and ip route for routes.

name: ss
tip: Modern replacement for many netstat use cases.

name: ping
tip: A failed ping does not always prove the host is down; ICMP may be filtered.

name: dig
tip: Use +short for concise output.

name: nmcli
tip: Distinguish devices from saved connections.

name: curl
desc: Transfer data and test services using URLs.
tip: -I requests headers; -O keeps the remote filename.

name: lsblk
tip: -f adds filesystem type, label, and UUID.

name: blkid
tip: UUIDs are commonly used in /etc/fstab.

name: df
tip: -i checks inode exhaustion, which can occur even when blocks remain.

name: du
tip: df reports filesystem totals; du measures files and directories.

name: mount
tip: Mount options can block execution even when permissions allow it.

name: fsck
tip: Usually run on an unmounted filesystem.

name: pvcreate
tip: LVM order: PV → VG → LV → filesystem.

name: vgcreate
tip: A volume group pools one or more physical volumes.

name: lvcreate
tip: Create a filesystem after creating the LV.

name: lvextend
tip: -r grows the filesystem with the LV when supported.

name: getenforce
tip: It reports Enforcing, Permissive, or Disabled.

name: setenforce
tip: This is not persistent across reboot.

name: restorecon
tip: Use after moving or creating content where policy expects a specific label.

name: semanage
tip: Pair fcontext changes with restorecon.

name: podman
tip: Podman is daemonless and commonly used on Red Hat systems.

name: crontab
tip: Cron fields are minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week.

name: at
tip: Use cron for recurring tasks and at for one-time tasks.

name: ssh
tip: Check permissions on private keys and host-key prompts.

name: scp
tip: Use rsync when efficient synchronization or resume behavior matters.

name: modprobe
desc: Load or remove kernel modules with dependency handling.
tip: Prefer modprobe over insmod when dependencies matter.

name: lsmod
tip: Use modinfo for module metadata.

name: sysctl
desc: Read or change runtime kernel parameters.
tip: Persistent settings belong in sysctl configuration files.
